opportunity: kuna's DWARF pass applied parameter names/types only to functions whose name had no `::` or `<` — a perfect split measured on a purpose-built C++ probe binary
test_name: kuna-console verify_cppproto (7 two-pass e2e assertions) + whole-binary decompile-all sweeps
inspiration: Ghidra DWARFFunctionImporter / DIEAggregate (a definition DIE fused with its DW_AT_specification declaration), DWARFName (the namespace path), DWARFDataTypeImporter (DW_TAG_class_type mapped like a structure, a reference like a pointer)
root_cause: NOT name-vs-address binding as first hypothesized. An out-of-line C++ member or namespace DEFINITION carries no DW_AT_name of its own — the name lives on the DW_AT_specification declaration — so `snap.name.is_empty()` dropped the DIE whole (name, prototype AND stack locals) before any binding was attempted. Name-keyed prototype binding is a SECOND, independent defect that the template cases expose: kuna files the demangled `maxof<int>` as `maxof`, and a qualified name lives in a nested scope the global by-name query never reaches.

speed.note: The DWARF walk itself runs identically with the gate on or off (the C++ facts are always computed, then dropped at commit when off), so the only marginal cost is committing them. The min-of-15 interleaved deltas are the trustworthy numbers on a box running concurrent agents: +1.72% on the witness and -0.83% on the C guard, both well inside the +5% budget. Single-shot medians swing wildly with load (an early fmt run reported +38.6% and did not reproduce in four re-runs), and where the on side is genuinely faster it is because a locked prototype skips output-trial recovery.

regglobal_fmt_x86_64 (real C, coreutils.classification: all 9 are improvements: `void *` parameters resolved to their real pointee (`char **authors`, `int8 *pn`, `uint8 *val`, `__mbstate_t *ps`) once transparent qualifier hops stopped consuming the type-mapper depth budget, plus one DWARF parameter name (`bool same_paragraph`)

cpp probe -O0 (C++ with STL, g++ -O0 -g).classification: member/namespace/template functions recover `this` + parameter names + types; one mangled name (`_ZSt14__relocate_a_1I...`) is replaced by its DWARF qualified name

cpp probe -O2 (C++ with STL, g++ -O2 -g).classification: all improvements (`Shape *`/`Account *`/`Circle *this` parameters and their DWARF names)

sweeps.measured_on: rebased onto main @1cff8ecb (PR #262); BOTH arms re-captured on the rebased tree, so #262's C++ call-site renames are in the baseline and do not pollute the diff

regressions_found_and_fixed_by_the_sweep: GCC IPA clone: `put_word.isra.1` (coreutils fmt, 0x23d0) is a nameless subprogram whose DW_AT_abstract_origin points at `put_word`, and whose TWO formal parameters both link to the SAME source parameter `Word *w` (IPA-SRA split the aggregate). Chasing that link produced `put_word(Word *w,Word *w)` and pushed the wrong callee signature into `put_line`. Fixed by following DW_AT_specification only for the subprogram link.

Variadic-template arity: `std::vector<int>::emplace_back<int>` keeps its expanded pack argument inside a `DW_TAG_GNU_formal_parameter_pack` grouping DIE, not as a direct child. Reading only direct children locked a one-parameter signature and dropped the argument at every call site. Fixed by flattening the pack.

Zero-width by-value aggregate: a `DW_TAG_class_type` maps to a named OPAQUE type of size 0 (fields are the sibling increment), and a zero-width by-value parameter failed `std::vector<int>::_M_realloc_insert` outright ('dereferencing a null/sentinel space pointer'). Fixed by degrading any non-positive-size parameter type to an `undefined<n>` at the DIE's own byte size.

Anonymous-aggregate name collision: naming every unnamed struct `anon_struct` fuses unrelated types under one interned name, which the qualifier-strip made reachable in many more places. Fixed by naming an anonymous aggregate after the typedef it was reached through (`__mbstate_t`, not `anon_struct`).
notes: Scope is function PROTOTYPES only. Struct/class FIELD population from DW_TAG_member/DW_AT_data_member_location is deliberately out of scope (a class stays a named opaque, so `this->balance` still prints as an offset); the seam for it is `build_datatype`'s struct/class arms, untouched by this change. `DW_AT_object_pointer` — the attribute Ghidra's ThisCallingConventionDWARFFunctionFixup uses to select `__thiscall` — is not acted on: kuna cannot register a `__thiscall` model yet (ProtoModel::decode is a stub), so the artificial `this` is passed as an ordinary first parameter, which is what the x86-64 SysV ABI does anyway.
